Last Shelter

Setting

The Last Shelter is the fugitive brotherhood’s hidden refuge. Aliya brings Kir and Kel here, but Khatul tests them before granting trust. The smith’s change of attitude after acceptance makes membership a tangible part of life in the community. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Feiruz’s last rescue

Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée Aliya. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before Brother Khatul. [6, 7, 8, 9, 2]

The ring and the brotherhood

Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how Brother Smith receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing Sahilia, rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. [3, 4, 10, 5, 11, 12, 13, 14]

Defending the Shelter and the ancient treaty

An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, Brainripper recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question. [15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22]
